codeReview.summary: The fix closes the prior blocking fail-open path. Instead of routing schedule-update checks through `get_stream_status()` and inheriting its degraded-runtime fallback to persisted DB state, `StreamService.update_stream_schedule()` now calls `StreamControlService.ensure_schedule_update_allowed()`, which directly inspects supervisor/systemd state and rejects future scheduling when managed-runtime liveness cannot be authoritatively verified for a stream that still has live indicators. The original overdue one-shot scheduler behavior from `4997a5a` remains intact, and the fix adds focused regressions for degraded supervisor and systemd inspection paths.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared environment note for DEV auth still documents the wrong fallback user ID, so workers can still lose time debugging auth identity conflicts during local API verification.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/library/environment.md:29` says unset `DEV_USER_ID` falls back to `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`, but `backend/app/api/deps.py:190-198` actually derives the fallback user ID from `uuid5(NAMESPACE_DNS, email)`. The fix transcript skeleton also shows a failed `/api/streams/{id}/status` verification attempt followed by reads of `backend/app/api/deps.py` to rediscover the real DEV auth identity.

summary: Pass. The managed-runtime reschedule guard now fails closed for degraded supervisor/systemd inspection and adequately addresses the original blocking review finding. No blocking correctness issues were found in the reviewed fix; one shared-state documentation mismatch remains around the default DEV auth user ID.
